attachments.origin_landmark: sacrum, iliac crest, lumbar transverse/spinous processes, common erector spinae tendon
attachments.insertion_landmark: transverse processes T1-T12 and ribs (thoracis); transverse processes C2-C6 (cervicis); mastoid process (capitis)

innervation.root_levels: segmental (C1-L5, matching level of each fascicle)

functional_compartments.name: Longissimus thoracis
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: dorsal rami, thoracic and upper lumbar levels
functional_compartments.function_note: Largest of the three erector spinae columns by PCSA; primary sagittal-plane extensor moment arm of the lumbar spine.
functional_compartments.source: Bogduk N, Macintosh JE, Pearcy MJ (1992) Spine 17(8):897-913 -- quantitative model of lumbar back muscle architecture and moment arms (erector spinae, multifidus, quadratus lumborum)

functional_compartments.name: Longissimus cervicis
functional_compartments.function_note: Long thin fascicles linking upper thoracic transverse processes to cervical transverse processes.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Longissimus capitis
functional_compartments.function_note: Longest, most superficial cervical extension of the column; inserts on the mastoid process alongside splenius capitis and SCM.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N, Macintosh JE, Pearcy MJ (1992) Spine 17(8):897-913 -- quantitative model of lumbar back muscle architecture and moment arms (erector spinae, multifidus, quadratus lumborum)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Longitudinal or transverse over the lumbar paraspinal mass, lateral to the spinous processes and medial to the transverse processes -- the paravertebral gutter. At the lumbar level the three erector spinae columns (iliocostalis lateral, longissimus middle, spinalis medial) are not reliably separable by ultrasound; the mass is usually treated as one compartment for injection purposes.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial to multifidus and the lamina/transverse processes; deep to the thoracolumbar fascia.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Vertically-striated muscle bulk running the length of the spine, thickest in the lumbar region; contracts on trunk extension.
structures_at_risk: dorsal rami of the spinal nerves running through the muscle mass
the lamina and spinous process deep to it, at the limit of a safe needle depth
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The only randomised controlled technique in the literature for this muscle group targets it as 10 bilateral intramuscular points equally distributed from L1 to L5 (0.4 mL/point), EMG-guided rather than ultrasound-guided. Included for the technique, not as an endorsement: this crossover trial (19 patients) found NO significant pain relief, functional, or quality-of-life benefit of 200 IU BoNT-A over saline at 30, 90 or 120 days for chronic low back pain -- a negative result that contradicts two earlier positive trials the authors discuss, and one this atlas records for that reason rather than omitting.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; de Lussanet de la Sabloniere M et al., BMC Musculoskelet Disord 18:454 (2017), doi:10.1186/s12891-017-1816-6 -- randomised, double-blinded crossover trial of paravertebral BoNT-A for chronic low back pain, the source of the injection technique described here (PubMed)

trigger_points.location_description: Longissimus capitis part only, near the mastoid process at about the C1-C2 level.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Behind and below the ear, sometimes spreading toward the eye.
trigger_points.notes: Documented only for the capitis part of this combined longissimus record; longissimus cervicis has no separately mapped trigger point in the source document.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999)
